summary: Return, in ascending order, every node from which all paths end at a terminal node (equivalently, nodes that cannot reach a cycle).
mainInsight: A node is safe exactly when it cannot reach a cycle. Reverse the edges and run Kahn's algorithm from the terminal nodes (out-degree 0): a node becomes safe when all its outgoing edges lead to safe nodes, i.e. its remaining out-degree hits 0.
invariant: A node enters the queue only once all of its original out-neighbours are already known to be safe.

commonMistakes: Running Kahn's algorithm on in-degrees of the original graph (that finds nodes not reachable from cycles, the wrong set).
Treating a self-loop node as safe.
Using plain visited DFS without the grey state, which cannot tell a cycle from a revisited safe node.
Forgetting to return the answer sorted.

promptVariants: Why reverse the graph before running Kahn's algorithm?
What does the reversed graph let you propagate?
options: Safety flows from terminals back to their predecessors
Reversing removes every cycle from the graph
In-degrees of the original graph mark safe nodes
It lets the BFS visit nodes in ascending order
cards.answer: Safety flows from terminals back to their predecessors
cards.explanation: A node is safe once all of its out-edges point to safe nodes. Reversed edges let a newly safe node notify its predecessors and decrement their remaining out-degree.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Reversing removes every cycle from the g: Cycles stay cycles; their nodes simply never reach out-degree 0.
incorrectOptionExplanations.In-degrees of the original graph mark sa: Original in-degrees answer a different question (reachability from sources).
incorrectOptionExplanations.It lets the BFS visit nodes in ascending: Order comes from the final scan, not from reversal.

promptVariants: Node 0 has a self-loop, node 1 points to node 2, node 2 is terminal. Result?
cards.explanation: Node 2 is terminal, so 1 (its only edge goes to 2) is safe. Node 0 loops on itself forever, so it is not safe.

incorrectOptionExplanations.[0, 1, 2]: The self-loop is a cycle; node 0 never reaches a terminal.
incorrectOptionExplanations.[2]: Node 1's only path goes to the terminal node 2, so it is safe too.

promptVariants: How does DFS with white/grey/black states find the safe nodes?
cards.answer: Mark a node grey on entry. If DFS reaches a grey node there is a cycle and every node on the current stack is unsafe. If all neighbours finish as safe, mark the node black (safe). Memoise results so each node is processed once: O(V + E).
cards.explanation: Same complexity; in Python watch the recursion depth with n up to 10^4.

promptVariants: What is the time complexity of the canonical code?
Derive the running time of Kahn's algorithm on the reverse graph.
cards.explanation: Building the reverse graph touches each edge once, each node is dequeued at most once, and each reverse edge is decremented once.

incorrectOptionExplanations.O(V * E): That is per-node searches without memoisation.
incorrectOptionExplanations.O(V^2): No pairwise node work; adjacency lists keep it linear.
incorrectOptionExplanations.O((V + E) log V): There is no priority queue; the output is ordered by a final linear scan.
